config.title: Default Props

intro.title: Default Props
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that displays a greeting message. You will learn how to use default props to provide fallback values for component properties when they are not explicitly passed. The core concept involves defining default values directly on the component to ensure it renders correctly even without all props. You will work with JavaScript functions, JSX for structure, and the defaultProps property in React. This helps make your components more robust and user-friendly by handling missing data gracefully.
intro.usecase: Default props are essential in React components that render UI elements with consistent fallback values when parent components don't provide specific props. In e-commerce product cards, default props ensure images display placeholder graphics when product images fail to load, and prices show "Price unavailable" when missing. Dashboard widgets use default props to render with standard colors and sizes when configuration data is incomplete. Form components rely on default props to show helpful placeholder text and validation messages even when custom labels aren't provided by parent forms.

objectives: Initialize default props for React components using static property definitions
Apply default props to functional components using ES6 default parameters
Configure components to render with fallback values when props are not provided
Manipulate component behavior by overriding default props with explicit values
Integrate default props with existing component logic to handle missing data gracefully
Construct reusable components with sensible defaults for common use cases
Update component implementations to use default props instead of conditional checks

steps.title: Create a functional component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Greeting that takes props as a parameter and returns null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The component should accept props as its parameter and return null.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Greeting component is defined that accepts props and returns null.
successCriteria: Greeting component is defined as a function that takes props and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Greeting component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your Greeting component accepts props and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named Greeting that takes props and returns null.

steps.title: Add JSX structure to the component
steps.instruction: Inside your Greeting component, return a JSX structure: a <div> containing an <h1> element that displays a greeting message using props.name.
steps.hint: The component should return JSX. Use props.name inside curly braces within the <h1> to display the name passed as a prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component returns a <div> with an <h1> that uses props.name to display a greeting.
successCriteria: The Greeting component returns JSX containing a <div> and an <h1> that uses {props.name}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component returns a <div> with an <h1> that uses {props.name} to display the greeting.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't yet return the required JSX structure. Ensure it returns a <div> containing an <h1> that uses props.name.

steps.title: Export the component
steps.instruction: Export the Greeting component as a default export so it can be used in other files.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax followed by the component name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component is exported as the default export, making it available for import in other files.
successCriteria: The Greeting component is exported using 'export default Greeting'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using 'export default' followed by the component name 'Greeting'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't exported yet. Use 'export default Greeting' to make it available for import in other files.

steps.title: Create a defaultProps object
steps.instruction: Add a defaultProps property to the Greeting component and set the name prop to 'Guest'.
steps.hint: After the component definition, assign an object to Greeting.defaultProps with a name property set to 'Guest'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component now has a defaultProps property that provides a default value for the name prop.
successCriteria: Greeting.defaultProps is defined as an object with a name property set to 'Guest'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've set the name property to 'Guest' inside the defaultProps object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Make sure you're adding a defaultProps property to the Greeting component with the correct structure.

steps.title: Compose App: default name vs custom name
steps.instruction: Add an App component as the default export. In its return, render `<Greeting />` with no props (uses your default name) and a second `<Greeting name="Alice" />` (or another name) so you contrast defaultProps with an explicit prop.
steps.hint: First line: bare `<Greeting />`. Second line: same tag with `name="..."`. Use `export default App` only. The Output tab often auto-mounts the first `const` component (`Greeting`), so you may still see a single Guest—that preview quirk doesn't mean the two-instance pattern in App is wrong.
steps.expectedOutcome: App renders two Greeting elements: one relies on defaultProps for name, the other passes an explicit name.
successCriteria: App is the default export and its JSX includes `<Greeting />` with no props and a second `<Greeting />` with a name prop set to a custom string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. You need both a bare `<Greeting />` and a second one with `name="..."`, and `export default App`.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add App as default export, render `<Greeting />` with no props, then a second `<Greeting name="Alice" />` (or similar) in the same parent div.

steps.title: Add a second prop with default value
steps.instruction: Add a 'message' prop to the Greeting component's parameter list and set a default value for it in the defaultProps object.
steps.hint: Add 'message' to the props parameter and update the defaultProps object to include a default message string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component now accepts a 'message' prop with a default value defined in defaultProps.
successCriteria: The Greeting component's props parameter includes 'message' and the defaultProps object contains a 'message' property with a string default value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added 'message' to both the props parameter and the defaultProps object with a string value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The goal is to add a 'message' prop to the component and provide a default value in defaultProps.

steps.title: Update JSX to use the new prop
steps.instruction: Inside the Greeting component, update the JSX to display both the name and message props.
steps.hint: Access props.message in your JSX, similar to how you access props.name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component will display both the name and message props in its JSX output.
successCriteria: The JSX includes both props.name and props.message, and the component returns valid JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying both props.name and props.message in the JSX. Check that your component returns valid JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The JSX doesn't seem to display both props correctly. Remember to access props.message in your JSX, similar to how you access props.name.
